# AGENTS.md (Grok Build)

Rules for Grok Build sessions, generated from `agent-policies` 0.2.0. Grok Build's exact config paths are not yet confirmed; place this file at the project root until they are.

## Rules

- `OWN-1` Write only your own paths. A bot writes only under paths it owns per the layout and `etc/registry.json`. Everything else is read-only to it. (enforced by: convention, auto-review)
- `OWN-2` Register before you write. A new bot or service is added to `etc/registry.json` (owner, paths, ports) before it creates files. (enforced by: convention)
- `ATOM-1` Atomic handoff. Write to a temp file in the same directory, then rename() it into place. Never let a reader see a partial file. (enforced by: convention)
- `SEC-1` No secrets on disk or in git. Never write secrets, tokens or environment values to `/workspace`, logs, memory or any repo. Never print environment variables. (enforced by: convention, auto-review, hook)
- `SEC-2` Secrets come from a secret store. Logins and API keys come from the environment's secret store (a vault or a masked secret request), never from files in a repo or workspace. (enforced by: convention)
- `LOG-1` Log every turn. Append one JSON line per turn to `var/log/<bot>/turns.jsonl` with `start`, `end`, `duration_s`, `tools`, `messages_sent`, `errors`. Log counts and metadata, never message content. (enforced by: convention)
- `RUN-1` Publish status atomically. At the end of each turn, write `run/<bot>/status.json` (temp then rename). (enforced by: convention)
- `CTX-1` Context hygiene. Read only what the task needs, page large files, prefer files and checkpoints over long chat context, and keep replies concise. (enforced by: convention)
- `GIT-1` No remote side effects without approval. No push, force-push, remote creation, history rewrite or hook bypass without explicit user approval. (enforced by: convention, auto-review, hook)
- `RET-1` Retirement is bounded. Retiring a bot touches only `bots/<bot>/`, `run/<bot>/`, `var/log/<bot>/` (moved to `var/archive/`) and its `etc/registry.json` entry. (enforced by: convention)
- `DOC-1` Lint-clean Markdown. Real headings (never bold as a heading), commands in fenced bash blocks, no emoji, plain words. markdownlint must pass. (enforced by: convention, hook)

## Principles

These apply to every agent in every environment. Rules in `policy.yaml` make them concrete.

### Do one thing well

Each bot has one role, one owned subtree and one log. Each script does one job. Compose them through files.

### Everything is a file

State, status, queues, metrics and config are plain files under `/workspace`. Anything a human or another agent needs to read is text: JSON, YAML, Markdown or Prometheus text format.

### Mechanism and policy are separate

`policy.yaml` says what must happen. Targets (skills, Cursor rules, hooks, Auto-review rules) are mechanisms that carry it out. Change policy in one place and regenerate.

### Least privilege by convention

All agents run as the same user, so the kernel cannot keep them apart. Each agent acts as if it had only the access its owned paths and its task need.

### Fail loudly, leave no partial state

Write temp then rename. If a step fails, stop and report it; do not route around a block.

### Plain, concise communication

Say what was done, what was not, and what is unverified. Skip filler.

## Best practices

### Context hygiene

- Read only what the task needs; page large files instead of dumping them.
- Put long results in files and reference the path.
- Before a long session fills the window, write a checkpoint to `docs/checkpoint-<date>.md` with intent, decisions, open questions and the next step.

### Files and paths

- Write only under paths you own (`bots/<bot>/`, `run/<bot>/`, `var/log/<bot>/`, plus entries in `etc/registry.json`).
- Hand work to another bot by writing a temp file and renaming it into `var/spool/<queue>/`.
- Keep scratch in `tmp/` and assume it can vanish.

### Logging

- One JSON line per turn in `var/log/<bot>/turns.jsonl`: `start`, `end`, `duration_s`, `tools`, `messages_sent`, `errors`.
- Log counts and metadata, not message content or personal data.

### Secrets

- Never print, copy or commit environment values or secret files.
- Ask for an API key through a masked secret request; use logins through the environment's vault.

### Writing

- Lint-clean Markdown: real headings, never bold as a heading.
- Put every command in a fenced `bash` block.
- No emoji. Plain words. Times in America/Los_Angeles with a zone label.

### Changes

- Reversible work proceeds; anything external (send, post, push, purchase, delete outside the box) waits for explicit approval.
- Test before claiming done, and say what was not verified.
